newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps -April gas oil trades at $26.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps -April gas oil trades at $26.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps rose sharply late afternoon on Monday on market perception that recent physical purchases by one local trader will be extended into the rest of this week, traders said.
"The market is firming because earlier people thought the physical purchases were short term but now they are not so sure," one trader said.
April gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.95/$26.05 per barrel compared with Friday's $25.40/$25.60.
April traded earlier in the day at $25.80, $25.95 and $26.00 per barrel, brokers said.
Firmer prices were also seen for the front month March where deals were seen at $27.00, $27.05 and $27.10 per barrel, up about 40 cents from Friday.
May was last quoted at $25.20/$25.40 from Friday's $24.80/$25.00.
Traders said rising prices were also due to tight supplies in Singapore where most refiners do not have any March or early April barrel available for spot sale.

Frimer prices were partly due to bullish sentiment brought on by stronger crude prices where on Friday May Brent closed up 32 cents to $19.74 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange while April gas oil ended up 25 cents per tonne to $160.50.
Fuel oil swaps also rose in active trading due to the firmer crude prices with April traded at $97.50 and $97.75 per tonne, brokers said.
April was last quoted at $97.50/$98.75 from Friday's 96.50/$97.50.
